Directions: Read the information below and use it to answer each question that follows.
Context: The following section focuses on composters and the movement of matter in a garden.
Content: Students grew vegetable plants in their school's garden. They learned that waste from the vegetables can be composted.
When vegetable waste is placed in a composter, bacteria help turn the waste into compost over time. The compost can then be used in a garden.
The students made this model to show how matter moves through a composter and a garden.
The students designed and built `text(two)` composter prototypes. The diagrams show the designs of the `text(two)` prototypes.

Composter `1` has wooden sides and its top is open to the air. The vegetable waste in the composter is mixed once a `text(week)`, which exposes the waste to air. Composter `2` has sides made of wire mesh and a wooden divider that creates `text(two)` separate sections. All the vegetable waste is `text(first)` placed in `text(one)` section. After a `text(week)`, the vegetable waste is moved to the other side of the divider. As the vegetable waste is moved from `text(one)` side to the other, it is mixed and exposed to air.
